GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
Examples of side effects include direct expenditures, sending emails, deleting files on a user's computer, modifying external documents, making tool requests that contain sensitive user data, expanding permissions to systems or data, delegating to a sub-agent, and even simply generating tokens may technically consume the user's time and money.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  - side_effect_examples: The list of example side effects given in the control side effects section.

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - root_authority: Rules in the #control_side_effects section carry root authority.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l461_608_n015' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L0533-L0542:
Examples of side effects include:

- Direct expenditures (e.g., ticket purchases)
- Sending emails
- Deleting files on a user's computer
- Modifying external documents (e.g., via POST requests)
- Making tool requests (including web GET requests) that contain sensitive user data
- Expanding permissions to systems or data
- Delegating to a sub-agent (which may itself incur further side effects)
- Even simply generating tokens may technically consume the user's time and money
